title: O Level English oral exam on 15 July 2026: reported prompt discrepancies and what SEAB found
asked: Ms Hany Soh asked whether the Ministry will review how the O Level English oral examination is conducted, after the 15 July 2026 session, and whether SEAB received requests for help from students or parents over the reported prompt discrepancy. Mr Low Wu Yang Andre asked whether SEAB will compare that session's scores against other sessions before results are finalised, and what remedies apply if a session-level or centre-level anomaly is found.
asked_by: Ms Hany Soh, Mr Low Wu Yang Andre and Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
response: Dr Janil Puthucheary set out the oral examination process: candidates see the instructions, text prompt and video on screen for 10 minutes of silent preparation, then the oral examiner reads out the same text prompt. He said SEAB's checks of the e-Examination system, digital logs and cybersecurity found no system malfunction, no cybersecurity incident and no discrepancy in the prompt displayed to candidates and examiners, with 432 candidates from 102 schools reporting issues out of close to 5,000 who sat that day. Preliminary data shows the mean oral score on 15 July was comparable to the other four 2026 sessions, and the mean score of the 432 reporting candidates was comparable to the rest. Schools are helping affected candidates apply for special consideration, and SEAB will review the oral examination processes so students read the prompt more carefully during the 10-minute preparation time.

key_points.point: Candidates get 10 minutes at the silent preparation station to plan their oral presentation, viewing instructions, a text prompt and a video on screen.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: They are given 10 minutes at this station to prepare a planned response to their oral presentation.

key_points.point: The approved prompt for the planned response segment was about who would go to a place like the one in the video for a haircut.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Who do you think would go to a place like this for a haircut? Why do you say so?

key_points.point: On the day, 173 candidates from 76 schools reported a different prompt on their screen; this later rose to 432 candidates from 102 schools.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the number of candidates who reported similar issues concerning the 15 July oral examination increased to 432 from 102 schools

key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: There was no evidence of a system malfunction.

key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: There was also no cybersecurity incident detected.

key_points.point: GovTech audited the technical platforms and processes and reached the same conclusion as SEAB.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: we have had GovTech come in to audit the technical platforms

key_points.point: Some candidates' contemporaneous planning sheets showed they had misread the prompt and then corrected themselves.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the student having written down what they thought originally what is the prompt, and then crossing that out and then writing the correct prompt

key_points.point: Preliminary data shows the mean oral score on 15 July was comparable to the other four 2026 sessions.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the mean score for the oral examination on 15 July is comparable to that of the other four sessions in 2026

key_points.point: Schools are working with affected candidates to apply for special consideration.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Schools are working with these candidates to apply for special consideration.

key_points.point: Applicants for special consideration will be updated and engaged on the process, which is still ongoing.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the applicants for special consideration will be updated and engaged on the process

key_points.point: Examiners use positive marking, looking at vocabulary, sentence structure, grammar, tense and how ideas are presented and built on.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The examiners are trained in a process of positive marking.

key_points.point: SEAB will review the oral examination processes so students read the oral prompt more carefully during the 10-minute preparation time.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: SEAB will review the oral examination processes for students to read the oral prompt more carefully during the 10-minute preparation time.

left_open: The number of irregularity reports filed by SEAB's own oral examiners and presiding officers concerning the 15 July English oral examination.
Whether anyone outside SEAB will be allowed to examine the login logs, examiners' marking comments, planning sheets and session audio.
Whether accurately processing a question under exam pressure is a skill assessed in the oral examination, and how students are prepared for it.
Whether terminals kept their own local logs of what was displayed on individual candidate screens.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered special consideration applications, terminal-level logging, prompt wording and user testing, and whether an external party could review the evidence.
